name: VARoleDiagnosticianKitchenApplianceMalfunction

custom.system_prompt: Chen and Yue's oven has started heating unevenly, ruining a couple of recent bakes. They ask Sigma to help figure out what's actually wrong before deciding whether to repair or replace it. Sigma narrows the cause through targeted questions.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Kitchen, evening, oven timer beep, faint smell of a slightly burnt bake

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Chen and Yue's oven has started heating unevenly, ruining a couple of recent bakes — one side browns much faster than the other. They ask Sigma to help figure out what's actually wrong before deciding whether to repair or replace it. Sigma asks whether it's a gas or electric oven, whether the unevenness is consistent or varies, whether there's a visible heating element issue, and how old the oven is, narrowing toward a likely cause and whether repair makes sense. Keep every line short and natural.

user1.name: Chen
user1.tts_prompt: Methodical, treats this like a bug to debug

user2.name: Yue
user2.tts_prompt: A little frustrated about the ruined bakes

variations.context: Couple troubleshooting an oven that's started heating unevenly, ruining recent bakes

setting.mood: Mildly frustrated about the ruined food, curious about the mechanism
setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple working through a shared kitchen problem together
setting.background: The oven is a few years old and this unevenness is new within the past week or two
setting.conversation_style: Short, practical exchanges, Chen treating it methodically, Yue more focused on the practical impact

scenario_template.topic: Chen and Yue compare notes on the uneven heating and which recent bakes it ruined, agreeing it's a real and recent problem. A couple of short lines.
scenario_template.note: They're frustrated at the oven, not each other.

scenario_template.topic: Chen asks Sigma to help them figure out what's actually wrong before deciding whether to repair or replace the oven, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, our oven's heating unevenly and ruined two bakes this week. Help us figure out what's actually wrong.'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks whether it's gas or electric, and whether the unevenness is consistent (always the same side) or varies, narrowing between a mechanical heating-element issue and something else.
scenario_template.note: Answers should be specific, e.g. electric, and consistently the same side is undercooked.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks whether they can see the heating element on the affected side glowing evenly when it's on, and roughly how old the oven is, narrowing toward a specific likely cause and informing whether repair is economical.
scenario_template.note: This should reveal something concrete, e.g. the element on one side doesn't seem to glow as brightly, and the oven is about six years old.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma explains that a dimmer, uneven-glowing element strongly suggests a failing heating element on that side, which is a relatively inexpensive and common repair for an oven this age, rather than needing full replacement, and suggests checking the model number for a compatible replacement part.
scenario_template.note: Sigma gives a specific diagnosis with a genuinely useful cost/repair implication, not just a vague guess.

scenario_template.topic: Chen and Yue agree to look up the part together, relieved it's a simple fix rather than needing a whole new oven. Keep this realistic — not fully confirmed until the part is ordered.

user1.name: Chen
user1.role: Analytical software developer, methodically troubleshooting an oven heating unevenly, treating it like a technical problem to debug. Speaks in short sentences. Satisfied by a specific, mechanistic explanation.

user2.name: Yue
user2.role: Creative food photographer, frustrated by ruined bakes from an unevenly heating oven. Speaks in short sentences. Relieved once a concrete, affordable fix is identified.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Diagnostician. Narrows an appliance malfunction through targeted questions (fuel type, consistency of the fault, visible element condition, appliance age) rather than guessing. Gives a specific diagnosis with a practical repair-versus-replace implication.

conversation_structure: The couple's initial observation is collaborative frustration at the appliance, not at each other
Sigma's questions narrow via fuel type, fault consistency, visible element condition, and appliance age
Sigma's diagnosis includes a practical repair-versus-replace implication, not just an abstract cause
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution is a specific, plausible diagnosis with a concrete next step, not full certainty until verified
assistant_behavior: Sigma gives a specific mechanistic explanation rather than a vague guess
Sigma connects the diagnosis to a practical decision (repair vs. replace)
